messages:
Alex: Heads-up — we have a ~18% p50 perf regression for Qwen2.5 on hosted-prod after the recent quant kernel swap. Repro on dedicated as well.

Maria: Ugh. Is this definitely the kernel swap or something else landed in the same window? Can you share the profile? :eyes:

Alex: Putting raw perf profile in the thread. Key suspects: RoPE scaling change we applied for long-context, new kernel selection heuristics that prefer fused matmul for multi-head attr, and KV cache alignment differences. perf-bot posted the flamegraph link: https://perf.internal/runs/1762345678/flame

perf-bot: New perf report uploaded: run=1762345678, model=qwen2.5, hw=A100-80G, batch_shapes=[1x2048,4x512], quant=A16->Q4f16, artifacts: /artifacts/1762345678.zip

Sanjay: Quick read: flame shows big regression in attention kernel time (+22%). Kernel selection log: we switched to `fused_attention_v2` for heads=64 paths when seq_len>1024. That code path does extra rotary scaling math — could be the RoPE change.

Kevin: Also saw KV cache hits misaligned: the cache stride changed after the kernel change. For some configs, kv_buffer_stride=128 -> 136 bytes and that kills L2 prefetch.

Jing: Tokenizer edge-case: multi-ling run with zh+en had ~3% extra tokens due to unicode normalization in the tokenizer update earlier this week. Not huge but contributes to overall token counts and batching shapes.

Alex: Repro script I ran:```
# repro quickbench
python infra/bench/repro.py --model qwen2.5 --seq 2048 --batch 1 --quant q4f16 --repeat 20
```
My numbers: baseline (before swap): p50=38ms p95=72ms; after: p50=45ms p95=93ms.

Maria: Nice minimal repro. Can you dump kernel selection debug? There's a flag `SERVING_KSEL_DEBUG=1` to log chosen kernels/alt paths.

Alex: Pasted excerpt from kernel log:
```
[2026-03-16T10:12:02Z] layer=7 heads=64 seq=2048 ks_choice=fused_attention_v2 rot_mode=rope_scale_v2 kv_stride=136
[2026-03-16T10:12:02Z] layer=8 heads=64 seq=2048 ks_choice=fused_attention_v2 rot_mode=rope_scale_v2 kv_stride=136
[2026-03-16T10:12:02Z] layer=9 heads=64 seq=2048 ks_choice=matmul_attention_v1 rot_mode=rope_scale_v1 kv_stride=128
```
Notice layer 9 falls back to matmul_attention_v1 — head/kv mismatch across layers.

Sanjay: That mismatch is bad. We assumed uniform kernel selection per model instance. Looks like kernel chooser is per-layer and uses local heuristics (seq, head_count, pos_embed) — and the rot_mode change makes different layers pick different kernels. Cache stride divergence probable cause of the L2 path thrash.

Kevin: Hypothesis: `rope_scale_v2` computes scaled sin/cos tables at runtime per-layer with 64-bit alignment, which shifts the KV buffer base for some layers. Lower-level allocator pads to 8B and combined with fused kernel's alignment requirements yields 136 instead of 128.

Jing: If that's true, we can try: a) force unified kernel choice across layers, b) make rotary table allocation come from a shared aligned pool, or c) revert rope_scale_v2 for qwen2.5 until we verify.

Maria: Can we A/B revert easily on hosted? If we pin model->kernel mapping in routing, we can roll back per-canary. Also need to check ALiBi experiments — did we enable ALiBi for some inference routes? ALiBi interacts oddly with RoPE in our code.

Alex: ALiBi was enabled in one traffic bucket last week as an experiment for long-tail perf. But the regression lines up with the kernel swap timestamp, not ALiBi enable. Still, ALiBi+RoPE codepath shares the same attention wrapper so worth checking.

Sanjay: I ran microbench of attention kernels in isolation. Results (seq=2048, heads=64): fused_attention_v2: 42ms, matmul_attention_v1: 36ms. But when run end-to-end with KV cache enabled fused v2 goes to 49ms — suggests worse cache locality.

Kevin: Attached allocation trace (snippet):```
alloc pool=kv_buf size=1048576 align=128 base=0x7f9a3c000000
alloc rope_table size=65536 align=64 base=0x7f9a3c010410  # misaligned => shifts next alloc
alloc kv_layer_7 size=262144 align=128 base=0x7f9a3c014000
```
We can see rope_table sized/padding inserted between pools.

Jing: Short-term mitigations: 1) patch allocator to always reserve rope_tables in a separate static region (no padding), 2) revert fused_attention_v2 kernel preference for heads=64 when seq>1024 to baseline. We should try 1 first (non-invasive).

Alex: Action plan: 
- Sanjay: run kernel microbench across shapes and produce a table per-heads/seq/quant by EOD.
- Kevin: prototype allocator patch and run the repro.
- Maria: prepare canary route to pin pre-swap kernel mapping for hosted, so we can rollback without model/version changes.
- Jing: confirm tokenizer normalization didn't skew batch shapes for repro (run with raw bytes).

Maria: I'll also scan rollout logs for ALiBi toggles and any other change ~1762345600..1762345800.

perf-bot: Scheduled job: 1762345678-kernel-matrix (expensive) queued on infra-2; ETA ~12m.

Sanjay: Early microbench results show fused_attention_v2 wins for seq<=512 but loses for >=1024 when KV enabled. So our heuristic must include kv_enabled flag.

Kevin: Good find. Could we incorporate a simple cost model: if kv_enabled && seq>1024 && heads>=64 -> prefer matmul_attention_v1?

Jing: Also check attention head vs KV head dims. Qwen2.5 has kv_heads=32 vs attn_heads=64 for some sharded configs; that mismatch requires head-splitting logic in GPU kernels and may be penalized in fused kernels.

Alex: Right. That explains why some layers (where kv_heads differ after remap) choose different kernels. We need kernel chooser to be aware of kv_head_count and head_dim mapping, not just attn_heads.

Maria: For rollouts: I'll prepare a canary that pins the old kernel mapping and a separate canary that pins new kernel but with allocator patch. Compare p50/p95 and error rates.

Kevin: I'll open a PR with allocator patch and a small unit test that validates base alignments across runs. Tagging @SRE for infra restart window.

Sanjay: I'll upload the kernel selection matrix once done: path=/artifacts/1762345678/kernel_matrix.csv

Alex: Thanks — let's reconvene after the matrix and the allocator patch. If we can get <5% difference with allocator fix, we can ship that + knob in kernel chooser for kv_enabled.

Jing: One more note: tokenizer multi-ling bug — if we see 3% token inflation, that affects batching distribution and can amplify perf regression in bucketed autoscaler. I'll send a fix to normalize-grapheme branch.

Maria: Perfect. Keep updates in this thread, and ping if you need quick rollback. :thumbsup:
